statement: Source dated 2024-11 reports: Flood losses relative to regional GDP are highest in Vayots Dzor, Tavush, Lori and Gegharkunik; the report also locates severe irrigation-water and land-degradation risks in high-poverty marzes.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-11 reports: Flood losses relative to regional GDP are highest in Vayots Dzor, Tavush, Lori and Gegharkunik; the report also locates severe irrigation-water and land-degradation risks in high-poverty marzes.

source_refs.locator: CCDR, Executive Summary, printed p. 7, and chapter 1, printed pp. 22–24, regional water, land and flood risks

uncertainty: Modeled flood-loss shares relative to regional GDP, not observed regional loss counts or a complete marz ranking; asset values affect estimates.

statement: Source dated 2024-11 reports: The CCDR links spatial disparities with fragility risks, notes high rural and border-region poverty, and says conflict with Azerbaijan raises risks across the economy; it does not identify climate change as causing conflict.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-11 reports: The CCDR links spatial disparities with fragility risks, notes high rural and border-region poverty, and says conflict with Azerbaijan raises risks across the economy; it does not identify climate change as causing conflict.

source_refs.locator: CCDR, chapter 1, printed p. 20, spatial disparities and fragility risks

uncertainty: The report does not establish a climate-to-conflict causal pathway.

statement: The 2020 communication's satellite-based assessment for 1984–2017 describes differentiated drought-related crop damage in the Ararat Valley, southwestern Gegharkunik, Kotayk and Gegharkunik. Its damage-frequency categories are not reused as current annual probabilities.
compact_statement: The 2020 communication's satellite-based assessment for 1984–2017 describes differentiated drought-related crop damage in the Ararat Valley, southwestern Gegharkunik, Kotayk and Gegharkunik. Its damage-frequency categories are not reused as current annual probabilities.

source_refs.locator: Fourth National Communication, printed pp. 93–94, satellite-based severe-drought damage frequency, 1984–2017

uncertainty: Historical satellite-derived damage categories; case, crop-loss and temporal denominators require method-specific interpretation.

statement: Source dated 2020 reports: By 2070, projected wheat yields fall about 19–20% in Ararat, Kotayk and Gegharkunik, potato yields 21% in Shirak, while wheat yields rise about 8% in Lori.
compact_statement: Source dated 2020 reports: By 2070, projected wheat yields fall about 19–20% in Ararat, Kotayk and Gegharkunik, potato yields 21% in Shirak, while wheat yields rise about 8% in Lori.
scenario: The yield tables describe climate-change projections without agrotechnical measures but do not identify the emissions pathway.

source_refs.locator: Fourth National Communication, printed pp. 93–94, Tables 5-7 to 5-9, yield projections by marz

uncertainty: The cited tables do not state the climate pathway; projections are not local production forecasts.

statement: Source dated 2020 reports: The communication records a crop-insurance pilot launched in 2018: potatoes and cereals against hail and frost in Shirak, and fruit and grapes in Armavir and Ararat.
compact_statement: Source dated 2020 reports: The communication records a crop-insurance pilot launched in 2018: potatoes and cereals against hail and frost in Shirak, and fruit and grapes in Armavir and Ararat.

source_refs.locator: Fourth National Communication, printed p. 138, pilot crop-insurance program

uncertainty: The report records launch and intended coverage, not enrollment, payouts or reduced losses.

statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The NAP identifies weak inter-agency coordination and information flows, poor climate integration in public bodies, and gaps in locally relevant risk data and local adaptation finance.
compact_statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The NAP identifies weak inter-agency coordination and information flows, poor climate integration in public bodies, and gaps in locally relevant risk data and local adaptation finance.

source_refs.locator: National Action Program, printed pp. 10–11, barriers to adaptation

uncertainty: The NAP describes baseline barriers from consultation, not a later institutional evaluation.

statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The 2021–2025 action list scheduled adaptation plans for pilot marzes Shirak and Tavush, then eight more marzes, integrating climate adaptation into regional development planning.
compact_statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The 2021–2025 action list scheduled adaptation plans for pilot marzes Shirak and Tavush, then eight more marzes, integrating climate adaptation into regional development planning.
institutions: Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure

source_refs.locator: National Action Program, printed pp. 30–32, measures 1.9–1.10 for marz adaptation plans

uncertainty: These were scheduled measures; the NAP does not verify their completion, and its 2025 deadline has passed.

statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The NAP says social norms can restrict women’s access to climate information, resources and opportunities, and calls for gender-responsive participation in adaptation decisions.
compact_statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The NAP says social norms can restrict women’s access to climate information, resources and opportunities, and calls for gender-responsive participation in adaptation decisions.

source_refs.locator: National Action Program, printed p. 19, principle on gender-responsive adaptation

uncertainty: The principle is generalized and is not a measured marz-specific gender gap.

statement: Source dated 2025-12-19 reports: The framework includes possible displacement among the human impacts of climate risks and places climate adaptation within a wider resilience and social-cohesion agenda.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-12-19 reports: The framework includes possible displacement among the human impacts of climate risks and places climate adaptation within a wider resilience and social-cohesion agenda.
scenario: UNSDCF 2026–2030 planning horizon; no climate scenario or displacement estimate is stated.

source_refs.locator: UNSDCF, printed pp. 23–24, climate risks and potential displacement in the framework rationale

uncertainty: Strategic potential-displacement framing in a framework, not climate attribution of a specific displacement event or violence.

statement: Source dated 2025-12-19 reports: The UN plans to rehabilitate conflict-affected farmland to reduce resource competition and pilot community-led restoration and efficient water use in border or displacement-affected municipalities to support livelihoods and social cohesion.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-12-19 reports: The UN plans to rehabilitate conflict-affected farmland to reduce resource competition and pilot community-led restoration and efficient water use in border or displacement-affected municipalities to support livelihoods and social cohesion.

source_refs.locator: UNSDCF, printed pp. 45–46, climate adaptation and planned community resilience measures

uncertainty: These are planned measures; the framework does not name pilot municipalities or report results.

statement: Source dated 2024-10 reports: Lori and Tavush hosted 7% of Nagorno-Karabakh refugees before the May 2024 floods; refugees and host households in Tashir and Alaverdi faced flood-related displacement and damage to homes, food supplies and essential services.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-10 reports: Lori and Tavush hosted 7% of Nagorno-Karabakh refugees before the May 2024 floods; refugees and host households in Tashir and Alaverdi faced flood-related displacement and damage to homes, food supplies and essential services.

source_refs.locator: May 2024 flood PDNA, printed pp. 35–36, Human Impact and Livelihoods

uncertainty: Historical PDNA context: the 7% refugee-hosting share concerns Lori and Tavush together before the May2024 flood, not each locality or current populations; host and refugee flood impacts are not conflict attribution.

statement: Source dated 2024-10 reports: Field discussions in Lori and Tavush found women-headed households more likely to miss flood compensation when homes or livelihood assets lacked official property registration.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-10 reports: Field discussions in Lori and Tavush found women-headed households more likely to miss flood compensation when homes or livelihood assets lacked official property registration.

source_refs.locator: May 2024 flood PDNA, printed p. 38, Gender Insights from affected communities

uncertainty: Focus-group/field-discussion account of registration-related compensation barriers for women-headed households; missing disaggregated data preclude a measured prevalence.

statement: Source dated 2024-10 reports: Flooding damaged eight hydrological stations in the Debed and Aghstev basins, impairing water monitoring; the PDNA calls for modern flood forecasting, risk modeling and early warning, especially in remote areas.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-10 reports: Flooding damaged eight hydrological stations in the Debed and Aghstev basins, impairing water monitoring; the PDNA calls for modern flood forecasting, risk modeling and early warning, especially in remote areas.

source_refs.locator: May 2024 flood PDNA, printed pp. 120–122, disaster-risk management impacts and recovery needs

uncertainty: Recommended upgrades are not evidence of completed works.
